text:
Daniil Tarasov has handed Todd McLellan a goalie decision, as one Yahoo Sports headline put it, and the numbers say he has earned the argument. Through 11 games he has allowed 19 goals on shots that would usually produce 30.6, which makes him the best goalie in the league per 60 minutes by goals saved above expected (the gap between goals allowed and what the shots usually yield). His .930 save percentage comes with a 4-4-2 record, which tells you how little help he gets some nights.

He's been good everywhere: .979 on low-danger shots, .800 on high-danger ones against a league .685. Detroit kept him in net for the centennial game against Boston, and The Hockey News quoted the room's view in a headline: "Dani's Provided That."

Now the honest part. Last season he finished minus-2.8 by our model over 33 games, and our talent range puts his true save rate near league average. Ten starts don't overturn that. The question is how long the run lasts, not whether it's real right now.
headline: Tarasov has made Detroit's net his argument
